subject: Dependency problem between shiny and html reference

messages.author: b9e26f275342e3c8
messages.subject: Dependency problem between shiny and html reference
parts:
I am attempting to develop a Shiny app that embeds the AutoDesk Viewer API https://developer.autodesk.com/api/view-and-data-api/ among other things. It seems that I am running into a dependency problem that I suspect has to do with jquery, as both Shiny and AutoDesk depend on it. Has anyone had a similar issue before? Know that I am a complete noob at jquery, so apologies if this question seems lame. 

To run a reproducible example:

runGitHub('paulgovan/AutoDeskR')

To check out the code:

https://github.com/paulgovan/AutoDeskR

server.R

library(shiny)
library(leaflet)

data <- data.frame(lat = 30.6190, long = -96.3359)

shinyServer(function(input, output, session) {

  output$map <- renderLeaflet({
    leaflet(data) %>%
      addTiles() %>%
      addCircleMarkers() 
  })
})

ui.R

library(shiny)
library(shinydashboard)
library(leaflet)

dashboardPage(dashboardHeader(title = "AutoDeskR"),
              dashboardSidebar(
                sidebarMenu(
                  menuItem("Map", tabName = "map", icon = icon("globe")),
                  menuItem("Drawing", tabName = "drawing", icon = icon("file-image-o"))
                  )
              ),
              dashboardBody(
                tabItems(
                  tabItem(tabName = "map",
                          fluidRow(
                            box(
                                leafletOutput("map")
                            )
                          )
                  ),
                  tabItem(tabName = "drawing",
                          fluidRow(
                            box(
                                tags$body(includeHTML('www/template.html')),
                                tags$body(includeHTML('www/viewer.html'))
                            )
                          )
                  )
                )
              )
)

template.html

<script src="jquery.min.js"></script>
<script src="jquery-ui.min.js"></script> 

<link href="style.css" rel="stylesheet"/>
<script src="three.min.js"></script>
<script src="viewer3D.min.js"></script>

<script>
  var viewablePath = [{"path":"1/V5-3110001.svf","name":"Scene"}];

  var viewer = null;
    $(document).ready (function () {
      var options = {
        'docid': viewablePath[0].path,
          'env': 'Local'
      };

      viewer = new Autodesk.Viewing.Private.GuiViewer3D($("#viewer-local")[0], {});
        Autodesk.Viewing.Initializer (options, function() {
 viewer.initialize();
          viewer.load (options.docid) ;
 });
      });
</script>

viewer.html

<div id="viewer-local" style="height:75vh; position:relative; overflow: hidden;"></div>

In template.html you can see my js dependencies. All html, css, and js dependencies are placed in the www directory. Note that 1/V5-3110001.svf in template.html above is the path to the AutoDesk model object.

messages.author: ca443e6eaa0e78ed
messages.subject: Re: Dependency problem between shiny and html reference
parts: I would start by just dropping the jquery reference from your template (and if you're seeing double jqueryui references in your browser's developer tools, then try dropping jqueryui as well). If you intended to wrap up this functionality as a reusable R package, then it would be worth talking about some of the more formal ways of declaring HTML dependencies that let Shiny resolve all the various libraries that different components want to load, and do the right thing--but if this is just for a one-off project, then it's totally fine for template.html to just "know" that jquery will already be loaded.

messages.subject: Re: Dependency problem between shiny and html reference
parts:
Thanks Joe! I ended up converting the jquery functions to plain javascript and removed the jquery/jquerui references (which I doubt jquery experts would agree with). Then I included the html with the great new htmlTemplate function, which was a breeze, but I still seem to be having a dependency problem. Note that originally I had built a simple ui in html as described here and everything seemed to work well. I am starting to wonder if that would be the better route. 

runGitHub('paulgovan/AutoDeskR')

And my end goal is to make an htmlwidget out of the AutoDesk API, which I think would be really cool. Though I don't have alot of javascript experience, so I'm slowly getting there :)

Thanks again,
Paul
